codeReview.summary: Clean implementation of three lifecycle hooks (on_init, on_update, on_shutdown) on ApplicationBuilder. Type aliases are pub(crate), fields are pub(crate) on Application, builder methods use consuming-self chaining pattern, hooks are wired into the correct call sites (run(), RedrawRequested, cleanup_on_exit()), and .take() is correctly used for FnOnce hooks. 8 unit tests cover storage, chaining, delta time correctness, and World mutation. All workspace tests pass, clippy clean, formatted.

issues.description: on_init hook is only invoked in run(), not in init(). If a user calls build() + init() separately (the documented alternative to run()), the on_init hook silently does not fire. The run() docstring does document this behavior ('Equivalent to build(), init(), on_init callback, and event_loop.run_app()'), but the method name on_init could mislead users into expecting it fires after any init path. Consider renaming to on_run or documenting the limitation more prominently in the on_init() doc comment.

summary: The implementation fully matches the feature description. Three lifecycle hooks are added to ApplicationBuilder with proper type aliases (pub(crate)), stored on Application, and wired into the correct call sites. The code follows project conventions: pub(crate) visibility, no unwrap in production, proper error handling, consuming-self builder pattern, formatted code, and zero clippy warnings. 8 unit tests provide good coverage of the builder API. One non-blocking observation about on_init only firing in run() (documented but potentially confusing). Two shared-state observations about frame order docs and TDD skill guidance.
